title: Three years at La Conga
summary: He explains how his band replaced the house band and stayed three years and two months.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I (inaudible) stay in that club seven, eight months, I call him one day. He used to stop the people from dancing, and got into the mike, said, now, (inaudible) something. I hate to interrupt you because you deserve this, and they deserve this too. (Inaudible) you've been dancing. But I wanted you to really appreciate this band. I want you to just dedicate a half an hour. Let them play some of their music, and I don't want you to dance, but to listen to the music they've got. So listen to really appreciate it, because they deserve. That's how much enthusiasm we got with the band.

So he used to (inaudible) high, and he have his band. I say, when the job -- why don't you get rid of your band? The people here, they're coming in. They want to dance, laugh and music. They want me. And when I stop playing, they know they've got to wait one hour. They start leaving, man. Why don't you put another (inaudible) in here? You don't need your band here no more (inaudible) good idea, so he got rid of his band.

So I brought -- I think I brought -- I think I brought (inaudible). And he said to me, from now on you're in charge of the thing, and I don't want nothing to do with (inaudible), nothing. Well, you rehearsed the act. If you

think the act ain't no good, don't open. I back you up, whatever you say. And (inaudible). So we (inaudible) close in that club, three years and two months. He go (inaudible) 8:00 o'clock, and they go mopping up with a name, they call a number (inaudible) club.
